page.layout: One column of running text. Below its last line, at the right, a short reference line "Gal.5.", set inside the text block and not a marginal note.

main_text.p: Affingunt illi cornua, propter ferociam & in faniam ebriorum. Comites eius recensent Satyros, Silenos, Salios, Priapos, Senidas, Phallos, &c. Pythagoras quoque, sicut & Anacharsis, interrogatus, quomodo quis fugere ac euitare posset ebrietatem? respondit: Si frequenter tecum in animo volueris & reuolueris, quae ebrius facis, vel infpexeris ea, quae alij ebrij faciunt. Plato temulentiae dicitis fuadebat, ut poti ad speculum fese contemplarentur, ita fore, ut ab eo vitio recederent, confpecta foeditate. Perpendat quisquis etiam illa verba, quae manus adpinxit parieti in conuiuio Balthafaris, Dan. 5. & congnoscet, ebrietatem nos priuare omnibus virtutibus: quas si Deus velit numerare, nullas reperiet in ebrio. Wenn wein eingeht/ so geht witz aus. Si velit ebrium probare impositum librae, nullam inueniet grauitatem, quae vel minimum faciat momentum Christiano dignum, fonder wirtals ein Bößwicht erfunden. Regnum coelefte ab illo seiungitur, & sobrietatis candidatis attribuitur. Deniq; magnae sunt vires vini, ut est 3. Efd. 3. imo ignea vis vini, teste Basilio, quam primum corpore humano fuerit immoderatius recepta, incendit ignita diaboli iacula. Nam vinum rationem & mentem demergit: at cupiditates & voluptates non secus ac oleum flammam, in flammat. Vnde non raro in scripturis haec duo peccata coniunguntur, videl. ebrietas & fcortatio: ut Hof. 4. Prouerb. 23. Rom. 13.Gal.5.

page.notes: The line "Wenn wein eingeht/ so geht witz aus." and "fonder wirtals ein Bößwicht erfunden." are in black letter; the second is a bold black-letter phrase, and "wirtals" may read "witz als" (uncertain). "& in / faniam" at the line end: the word is probably "insaniam" with its hyphen lost in the scan, so it is printed as seen. The page-number and "Gal.5." placement are read from the scan. Quoted scripture references are copied as printed (Efd. 3., Hof. 4., Prouerb. 23., Rom. 13.). "Vt" is written "ut" per the u/v rule. Long s is printed as plain s throughout.
